$comment: THE ONE CONSTANTS FILE. Every URL, name, tool, cap, quota, host step, troubleshooting row and doc citation in every other file of this repo is generated from here by scripts/build.mjs and pinned by test/mirror.test.mjs. Edit this file, run `npm run build`, commit the result. The tool list, the unkeyed tier, the caps, the host ids and the sign-in meta key are a MIRROR of resume-signal-pro/src/config/mcp-tools.ts (itself a mirror of supabase/functions/agent-mcp); re-sync `mirror` when that file changes. Step text carries {{placeholders}} the build fills from the constants — a number is never typed into a sentence.
description: Job search over employers' own hiring systems. Search with no key; a free key opens every read tool.

hosts.name: Claude
hosts.also: claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude on your phone
steps: In Claude, open **Customize**, then **Connectors**.
Click **Add custom connector**.
If it asks for a **Name**, type `{{displayName}}`.
Paste this address into **MCP server URL**: `{{url}}` — this address is on Supabase, the company that hosts our server; it is ours. Paste it exactly as it is.

If Claude asks about **Authentication**, choose **Sign in when needed**. If it asks about **OAuth client**, choose **Register automatically**. Claude may already show these as "Detected" — leave them. Do not choose **No sign-in**: Claude cannot change that later, so the tools that need your account would stay off until you remove the connector and add it again.
Click **Add**.
In a chat, click **+**, open **Connectors**, and switch **{{displayName}}** on.
Ask Claude: `Using {{displayName}}, call board_stats and tell me how many jobs are open right now.`
hosts.verify: Under **+ → Connectors**, {{displayName}} is on. Ask "call board_stats": the answer names the number of open postings and a note like "unkeyed: N of {{perAddressPerDay}} calls left today".
hosts.signInOn: the first time Claude needs your account — to open a posting in full, to check a shortlist, or to apply — a **Connect** card appears in the chat. Click it, sign in to {{displayName}}, press **Allow**, and Claude continues where it stopped.

hosts.name: ChatGPT
steps: In ChatGPT, open **Settings**, choose **Security and login**, and turn on **Developer mode**. If you do not see it, your account or workspace does not allow it yet.
Go to chatgpt.com/plugins and click the **+** button.
Type a name — `{{displayName}}` — and a description — `Live job board: search real openings from employers' own hiring systems.`

Under **Connection**, paste this address as the MCP server URL: `{{url}}`. Paste it exactly as it is — do not add `/mcp` at the end. The address is on Supabase, the company that hosts our server; it is ours.
Create the connection, and check the list of tools it found — there should be {{toolCount}}.
Start a new chat and add **{{displayName}}** from the tools menu.
Ask: `Search {{displayName}} for nurse jobs in Texas and show me the first ten.`
hosts.verify: Ask it to search for "nurse in Texas": {{searchRows}} results with ids come back. ChatGPT's own search uses `search` and `fetch` — {{searchRows}} results per search and the full text of any result — with no sign-in.
hosts.signInOn: if a tool needs your account, ChatGPT shows its sign-in for {{displayName}}; sign in and press **Allow**.

hosts.name: Claude Code
steps: Copy this line and run it in your terminal (`--scope user` makes it available in every folder, not just this one): `{{claudeCodeKeyless}}`
Start `claude` and type `/mcp` — `{{serverName}}` is listed as connected.
Ask: `call board_stats` — the answer names the number of open postings and says how many free calls are left today.
hosts.verify: `/mcp` lists `{{serverName}}` as connected; "call board_stats" answers with the count and the unkeyed note; with a key, "call key_status" names your tier and calls left.
hosts.signInOn: without a key, the first tool that needs your account makes `/mcp` show `! Needs authentication`; type `/mcp` and sign in in the browser (Claude Code 2.1.186 or newer can also run `claude mcp login {{serverName}}`).

hosts.name: VS Code

Or paste the block below into `.vscode/mcp.json`. When the server starts, VS Code asks for the key; press Enter to leave it empty and use the tools that need no key.

hosts.verify: When it prompts for the key, Enter leaves it empty; ask the chat "call board_stats".

hosts.name: Any other MCP client
steps: POST one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request to `{{url}}` (Streamable HTTP; no session to keep); the first one is the `initialize` message below.
Then ask your agent to call `board_stats`.
hosts.keyed: With a key, send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on each request; without one, {{anonToolsProse}} still answer.
hosts.verify: The `initialize` answer's `serverInfo.name` is `{{serverInfoName}}`; the **Test the server** button on {{agentsPage}} runs this for you.
hosts.signInOn: without a key, a tool that needs your account answers a sign-in challenge (HTTP 401); a client that supports sign-in opens it, and a client that does not needs a free key.

troubleshooting.symptom: Sign-in through this server is not switched on yet, so this tool needs a key.
troubleshooting.why: The tool needs your account, and sign-in from chat apps is not switched on today.
troubleshooting.fix: Search, board statistics and full postings still work with no key. To use every tool, connect from Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code with a free key ({{keyPage}}).
Click it, sign in to {{displayName}}, press **Allow**; Claude retries the call itself.

troubleshooting.symptom: Claude: "Couldn't reach the MCP server" or "Authorization with the MCP server failed"
troubleshooting.why: The address was mistyped, `/mcp` was added to it, or (when sign-in is on) the sign-in could not finish.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the address is exactly `{{url}}`; press **Test the server** on {{agentsPage}}; if the test says sign-in is on and the card still fails, remove the connector and add it again with **Sign in when needed** + **Register automatically**.

troubleshooting.why: A tool that needs your account was called with no key, and the server asked for sign-in.
troubleshooting.fix: Type `/mcp` and follow the browser steps (2.1.186 or newer: `claude mcp login {{serverName}}`), or add a free key with `--header`.

troubleshooting.why: Your network address used its {{perAddressPerDay}} free calls today; an office or a chat service counts as one address.
troubleshooting.fix: Get a free key at {{keyPage}} ({{dailyQuota}} calls a day, no account) and add it to your app. Resets at midnight UTC.

troubleshooting.why: The key was cut off, or the header lacks `Bearer ` with the space.
troubleshooting.fix: The header must read `Authorization: Bearer {{keyPrefix}}…`. A key is shown once; get a new one if lost (the old one stops working).

troubleshooting.why: A newer key was made for the same account or email; only the newest works.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the newest key, or make one more and update every app that holds the old one.

troubleshooting.why: The free key's day is spent.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for midnight UTC; the unkeyed tools still answer; an Agent Pass raises the limit for its hours.

troubleshooting.why: Too many calls in one minute.
Résumé fit scoring needs a paid key or a live Agent Pass.
troubleshooting.fix: {{keyPage}} for a paid key, or {{passPage}} — search keeps working.

troubleshooting.symptom: The apply agent needs an active Agent plan or a live pass.
troubleshooting.fix: {{passPage}} (sign in first), or the Agent plan on the site.

troubleshooting.symptom: No agent mandate on this account.
troubleshooting.why: The apply agent is not set up yet (the same answer names "Your agent is switched off." and "No resume on file" when that is the blocker).
troubleshooting.fix: Account → set up the apply agent: turn it on, choose countries and field, add the CV. The off switch always wins.

troubleshooting.symptom: The pass on this account is not live.
troubleshooting.why: The pass ended, or its applications are used ("No applications left on this pass.").
troubleshooting.fix: Search keeps working; buy another pass when the clock ends.

troubleshooting.symptom: That is not a job id from this board.
troubleshooting.why: You passed a link or a title.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the id from a search, e.g. `greenhouse:acme:12345`; the id in a `{{jobsPage}}?job=<id>` link is the same one.

troubleshooting.symptom: This is an MCP server for AI agents, not a web page
troubleshooting.why: You opened the address like a web page.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing is wrong. Paste it into your agent; the how-to is {{agentsPage}}.

troubleshooting.symptom: Cursor / VS Code / Cline: server listed, zero tools
troubleshooting.why: Wrong transport (Cline: not `sse`; VS Code: `"type": "http"`), or `/mcp` appended to the address.
troubleshooting.fix: The address ends in `/agent-mcp` exactly; the transport is HTTP (Cline: **Streamable HTTP**).

troubleshooting.symptom: ChatGPT only ever searches and fetches
troubleshooting.why: By design: ChatGPT's search calls `search` and `fetch`, {{searchRows}} results a page.
troubleshooting.fix: For filters (pay, remote, seniority), use an app that calls `search_jobs`.

troubleshooting.symptom: Sign in to use this tool
troubleshooting.why: A tool that needs a key was called with none (HTTP 401 from a script or curl).
troubleshooting.fix: Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (free at {{keyPage}}), or call one of {{anonToolsProse}}.

sentences: Navigate to **Customize > Connectors**
Click "Add custom connector"
**Name**: the display name shown in the connectors list.
**MCP server URL**: the HTTPS address where the server accepts MCP requests
**Sign in when needed**: Claude connects without credentials and prompts users to sign in when the server asks.
**No sign-in**: anyone with access to the server URL can use the connector.
**Register automatically**: Claude registers OAuth clients with the server as users connect (Dynamic Client Registration).
**Use Claude's published identity** (recommended): the server reads Claude's client details from a URL Anthropic hosts (Client ID Metadata Document). Nothing to set up; the server must support it.
After you continue, Claude checks the URL and pre-fills the authentication settings it detects, marked "Detected."
Use the "+" button in your chat interface to access "Connectors," where you can enable/disable connectors per conversation.
Authentication settings (OAuth credentials and request headers) can't be changed after a connector is added. To change them, remove the connector and add it again with the new details.
The two-step dialog described here is rolling out gradually.
Request header authentication is in beta and available to a limited set of organizations.
Most servers that use bearer tokens reject the second form.

If your registered MCP URL returns a 301/302/307/308 redirect to a different host … the Authorization header is dropped on the redirect … and the connection fails with 'Authorization with the MCP server failed'
Open **Settings**.
Select **Security and login**.
Turn on **Developer mode**.
Go to ChatGPT Plugins.
Select the plus button.
Enter a user-facing name and description.
Under **Connection**, choose the connection method: For a public endpoint, enter the MCP server URL, including the `/mcp` path.
Create the connection.
Review the tools and metadata discovered from the server.
Start a new conversation and add the MCP connection from the tools menu.
Declaring both `noauth` and `oauth2` tells ChatGPT it can start with anonymous calls but that linking unlocks privileged behavior.

Triggering the tool-level OAuth flow requires both metadata (`securitySchemes` and the resource metadata document) **and** runtime errors that carry `_meta["mcp/www_authenticate"]`. Without both halves ChatGPT will not show the linking UI for that tool.

ChatGPT does **not** support machine-to-machine OAuth grants such as client credentials, service accounts, or JWT bearer assertions, nor can it present custom API keys or customer-provided mTLS certificates.
